messages.subject: `mosaicsExample' package
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I would like to try your program on my Chip-seq dataset.
I want to learnhow to use it first on your example dataset. From the
http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/2.8/bioc/vignettes/mosaics/inst/doc/mosaics-example.pdf
I learned that it is contained in the `mosaicsExample' package.
I failed to install it:

install.packages("mosaicsExample")
Installing package(s) into ‘C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-212~1.1/library’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
Warning in install.packages :
  package ‘mosaicsExample’ is not available

By the way, the mosaics package could only be downloaded directly from
your site http://www.stat.wisc.edu/~keles/Software/mosaics/. The
download from the bioconductor failed due to the same error:

source("http://www.bioconductor.org/biocLite.R")
BioC_mirror = http://bioconductor.org
Change using chooseBioCmirror().
>     biocLite("mosaics")
Using R version 2.12.1, biocinstall version 2.7.7.
Installing Bioconductor version 2.7 packages:
[1] "mosaics"
Please wait...

Installing package(s) into ‘C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-212~1.1/library’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
Warning in install.packages :
  package ‘mosaics’ is not available

Thanks and I will appreciate any assistance,
Rita.

messages.subject: Re: `mosaicsExample' package
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rita,

Thanks for your interest in mosaics package and sorry for the
inconvenience.

(1) Solution # 1:

You can install "mosaics" and "mosaicsExample" packages using
"install.packages()" function but in this case, you first need to
select bioconductor in the list of repositories to be accessed. This
is because bioconductor is not chosen as accessible repositories by
default in R. You can change them in Packages > Select repositories in
the menu. Please highlight all of BioC * there and try:

install.packages("mosaics")
install.packages("mosaicsExample")

(2) Solution # 2:

"mosaics" and "mosaicsExample" packages are available from
Bioconductor ver. 2.8 (the most recent version is ver 2.9 which was
released last month). Your error message says that it trys to download
"mosaics" package from Bioconductor ver. 2.7. I think that this
problem might be fixed by changing options or using different
Bioconductor mirror.

(3) Solution # 3:

Alternatively, you can just download Windows binary
("mosaics_1.0.1.zip" and "mosaicsExample_0.99.3.zip") from the
following links:

http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/2.8/bioc/html/mosaics.html
http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/2.8/data/experiment/html/mosaicsExample.html

and install them by using Packages > Install package(s) from local zip
files... in the menu.

Thanks,
Dongjun

messages.subject: Re: perl script to preprocess eland output
messages.subject_clean: perl script to preprocess eland output
messages.body_plain:
HI Tim,

I am now actually preparing new version of mosaics package with significant improvents. I also have updated the perl script so that it can process popular aligned read file formats. You can download this new perl script ("process_readfiles.pl <http://process_readfiles.pl>") here:

http://www.stat.wisc.edu/~chungdon/mosaics/

This new perl script can process following file formats:
- eland result
- eland extended
- eland export
- bowtie default
- SAM
- BED

This perl script will be incorporated into the new version of mosaics
package. In the new version of mosaics package, you will be able to
process aligned read files within the R environment.

Command line:

> perl process_readfiles.pl <http://process_readfiles.pl> [file_format] [frag_len] [bin_size] [collapse] [infile_location] [output_location] [infile_name] [generate_by_chr]

You don't need to specify the chromosome to process with this new perl script and chromosomes will be automatically extracted from the aligned read file. For example, if you want to construct bin-level files (bin size = 50; will be exported to the current directory) from "bowtie_results.out" (bowtie file format; located in the current directory), where average fragment length is 200, the command line will be:

> perl process_readfiles.pl <http://process_readfiles.pl> bowtie 200 50 3 ./ ./ bowtie_results.out Y

Please try this new perl script for your bowtie file and let me know whether it works for you.

Thanks,
Dongjun

Hi Tim,

Based on the error messages you attached below, I guess that you clicked the link to "process_readfiles.pl <http://process_readfiles.pl>" after you opened the page "http://pages.stat.wisc.edu/~chungdon/mosaics/" (correct me if it is not the case). It you click the link to the perl script in your web browser, your web browser tries to "run" it instead of saving it. So please don't click the link to the perl script but instead save the perl script to your local drive using "Save Link As..." in the menu. If you still have the problem with downloading the perl script, I'll send it to you through e-mail instead.

Thanks,
Dongjun

  I downloaded the "process_readfiles.pl <http://process_readfiles.pl>" according to what you said, however that file contains nothing but the error message. Please send the perl script to me by email.

Thanks so much!
tim

It you click the link to the perl script in your web browser, your web browser tries to "run" it instead of saving it. So please don't click the link to the perl script but instead save the perl script to your local drive using "Save Link As..." in the menu. If you still have the problem with downloading the perl script, I'll send it to you through e-mail instead.

> Dongjun
